candidates.title: Scaling Managed Agents with stable interfaces
candidates.summary: Chapter 01 : Don’t adopt a pet Scaling Managed Agents : Decoupling the brain from the hands 01 Don’t adopt a pet 02 Decouple the brain from the hands 03 The session is not Claude’s context window 04 Many brains, many hands 05 Conclusion Published Apr 8, 2026 Team Engineering Topics Agents Claude Developer Platform Context engineering Tool use Safeguards See more... Related articles Announcements May 18, 2026 Anthropic acquires Stainless View more Get started with Claude Managed Agents by following our docs . A running topic on the Engineering Blog is how to build effective agents and design harnesses for long-running work . A common thread across this work is that harnesses encode assumptions about what Claude can’t do on its own. However, those assumptions need to be frequently questioned because they can go stale as models improve. As just one example, in prior work we found that Claude Sonnet 4.5 would wrap up tasks prematurely as it sensed its context limit approaching—a behavior sometimes called “context anxiety.” We addressed this by adding context resets to the harness. But when we used the same harness on Claude Opus 4.5, we found that the behavior was gone. The resets had become dead weight. We expect harnesses to continue evolving. So we built Managed Agents: a hosted service in the Claude Platform that runs long-horizon agents on your behalf through a small set of interfaces meant to outlast any particular implementation—including the ones we run today. candidates.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations — Google DeepMind
candidates.summary: October 27, 2026 EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations View publication Download Share Copied Abstract We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research. Your browser does not support the video tag. Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world. The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity. With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak. Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences.
